title: Sorrow
text:
Grigory Petrov, a turner known in his district as a master craftsman and also as the most worthless peasant there, was driving his sick old wife through a snowstorm to the hospital in town. She lay silent in the sledge. As he drove, he talked to her, to himself, to the doctor in his head, and he began to remember.

For forty years they had lived together, and in those forty years, he realized, he had been drunk, had quarreled with her and beaten her, and had never once shown her any tenderness. She had gone out begging bread for them and had been afraid of him the whole time. He began to plan how he would make it up to her: buy her a kerchief, treat her well, let her sit quietly at home.

He turned to look at her. The snow was not melting on her face. She was dead. And only now, too late, he felt how sorry he was for her.

He turned the sledge back toward home, but he lost the road in the storm and fell asleep in the snow. He woke in a hospital, with the doctor telling him his frozen hands and feet would have to be cut off. Grigory wanted to say something, to start his life over, but he could not.
lesson: Tenderness put off until later may never be given at all. Say and show the love you mean to your family now.
people: Grigory Petrov the turner, his wife, the doctor Pavel Ivanovich
